course.title: Italian B2 — Upper Intermediate
course.description: An upper-intermediate Italian course mapped to the CEFR B2 descriptors: defend an argument, follow complex media, write formal correspondence, and negotiate with nuance.

lessons.title: Advanced connectors & argumentation
lessons.grammar_note: Conditional connectors like *a patto che* and *purché* trigger the congiuntivo — they frame a condition, not a fact: *a patto che tu sia d'accordo*.

items.example: Costa di più; d'altro canto, dura molto più a lungo.
I dati erano incompleti; ciò nonostante, la decisione è stata presa.
Accetto l'incarico, a patto che i tempi siano realistici.
Per quanto riguarda il budget, ne discuteremo la settimana prossima.
Il progetto è insostenibile; in altre parole, va ripensato da zero.
Serve un intervento immediato, vale a dire entro questa settimana.

sections.heading: Beyond the present: imperfetto congiuntivo
sections.text: At B2 the subjunctive stops being a present-tense trick. When the trigger is in the past or the conditional, you need the *imperfetto congiuntivo*: *essere → fossi, fossi, fosse, fossimo, foste, fossero*; *avere → avessi, avessi, avesse, avessimo, aveste, avessero*; regular verbs add *-assi / -essi / -issi* (*parlassi, prendessi, dormissi*). Compare *penso che sia difficile* (present) with *pensavo che fosse difficile* (past). And *vorrei che tu fossi qui* — I wish you were here.

sections.heading: Concordanza dei tempi
sections.text: The tense of the main clause decides the subjunctive you use. A present or future opinion takes the present or past subjunctive: *credo che abbia ragione*, *credo che abbia avuto ragione*. A past or conditional opinion pulls everything one step back: *credevo che avesse ragione*, *vorrei che venisse*. Getting this agreement right is one of the clearest signals of a B2 speaker.

sections.heading: Congiuntivo passato & trapassato
sections.text: For completed actions inside a subjunctive clause, use compound forms. The *congiuntivo passato* is *abbia / sia* + participle: *è strano che non abbia chiamato*. The *trapassato congiuntivo* is *avessi / fossi* + participle and marks an action earlier than a past main verb: *pensavo che fosse già partito* — I thought he had already left. This tense is also half of the third-type hypothetical you will meet later.

sections.heading: New triggers to master
sections.text: Beyond *penso che*, B2 leans on subordinating conjunctions that always take the congiuntivo: *benché* and *sebbene* (although), *affinché* (so that), *a meno che (non)* (unless), *purché* and *a patto che* (provided that), *senza che* (without). *Benché fosse stanco, ha continuato a lavorare* — although he was tired, he kept working.

body.scenario: You are a guest on a lively current-affairs talk show. The host claims that smart-working has permanently damaged productivity and that companies were right to call everyone back to the office. You take the opposite view. Open with your thesis, back it with two concrete examples, concede one fair point, then rebut the host's strongest objection without losing your composure.
body.persona: A provocative but professional TV host from Turin who interrupts, reframes your words, and pushes back with 'ma non crede che…?'
body.goal: Sustain a nuanced argument for two to three minutes, using at least two advanced connectors and one 'benché' or 'sebbene' + congiuntivo, while conceding one point gracefully

lessons.title: The news & the media
lessons.grammar_note: News Italian runs on the passive: *è stato arrestato*, *sono stati pubblicati i dati*. Watch for *venire* as a passive auxiliary too — *viene trasmesso in diretta* means 'it is broadcast live'.

items.example: Ogni testata giornalistica ha una sua linea editoriale.
L'inchiesta del giornale ha portato alla luce un giro di tangenti.
Un buon giornalista verifica sempre le proprie fonti.
La notizia circola da ore, ma non sembra molto attendibile.
La disinformazione si diffonde più in fretta delle smentite.
I telegiornali hanno dato grande risalto allo sciopero.

sections.heading: Type 1 — la realtà
sections.text: The first hypothetical describes something realistic or probable: *se* + indicative in both clauses. *Se piove, resto a casa* — if it rains, I stay home. For a likely future, Italian happily uses the future in both halves: *se avrai tempo, ti chiamerò*. Nothing exotic here — but it is the baseline the other two types depart from.

sections.heading: Type 2 — la possibilità
sections.text: For an unlikely or purely imagined present, use *se* + *imperfetto congiuntivo* in the condition and the *condizionale presente* in the result: *se avessi più tempo, leggerei di più* — if I had more time, I would read more. *Se fossi in te, accetterei l'offerta* — if I were you, I would accept. This is the pattern for giving advice and speculating, and it appears constantly in negotiations and debates.

sections.heading: Type 3 — l'irrealtà
sections.text: For something in the past that did not happen, pair the *trapassato congiuntivo* with the *condizionale passato*: *se avessi studiato di più, avrei superato l'esame* — if I had studied more, I would have passed. Because it points at a closed, unchangeable past, this is the tense of regret, blame, and hindsight: *se me l'avessero detto prima, avrei cambiato programma*.

sections.heading: Mixing the types
sections.text: Real speakers blend the halves. A past cause with a present consequence is common: *se avessi accettato quel lavoro, ora vivrei a Roma* — if I had accepted that job (past), I would now live in Rome (present). And in casual speech Italians often collapse the second type into a double imperfect indicative — *se avevo tempo, venivo* — but keep the congiuntivo + condizionale form in any formal or written context.

body.scenario: You are freelancing and a client wants to sign you for a six-month project, but their opening offer is a fixed price with a tight deadline and no clause for extra revisions. Negotiate: justify a higher rate, propose a staged timeline, and secure a clause covering additional work. Stay collaborative — aim for an agreement both sides can accept.
body.persona: A courteous but budget-conscious project manager who counters every request with 'capisco, però il nostro tetto di spesa è questo' and only moves when you offer a concrete trade-off
body.goal: Reach a concrete compromise on price, timeline, and revisions, using at least one second-type hypothetical (*se potessimo… accetterei*) and diplomatic hedging

lessons.title: Nuance, register & hedging
lessons.grammar_note: *Eventualmente* is a false friend: it means 'if need be / possibly', never 'eventually'. For 'eventually' use *alla fine* or *prima o poi*.

items.example: Tutto sommato, la riunione è andata meglio del previsto.
A dire il vero, non ero del tutto convinto della proposta.
Eventualmente possiamo spostare la scadenza di qualche giorno.
Il direttore sostiene che i risultati siano più che soddisfacenti.
Non è mica facile trovare casa a Milano di questi tempi.
Consegneremo il lavoro venerdì, salvo imprevisti.

sections.heading: Register and openings
sections.text: A formal Italian letter chooses its salutation carefully: *Gentile* + name/title for a person you address courteously, *Egregio Dottore / Egregia Dottoressa* for greater formality, *Spettabile* + company for an organization. The whole text stays in the *Lei* form, capitalized in polite correspondence (*La contatto*, *Le scrivo*). A neutral opener sets the subject at once: *La contatto in merito a un ordine effettuato il 3 marzo scorso.*

sections.heading: Reporting the facts: passive & discorso indiretto
sections.text: Formal complaints lean on the passive to sound objective and impersonal — *il pacco è stato consegnato danneggiato*, *non mi è stato fornito alcun documento*. Reported speech shifts tenses back and moves to the conditional for a future-in-the-past: *mi era stato assicurato che il prodotto sarebbe arrivato entro cinque giorni* — I had been assured the product would arrive within five days. This distance is exactly the tone a complaint needs.

sections.heading: Making the request diplomatically
sections.text: State what you want without aggression, using the conditional and the congiuntivo: *Le sarei grato se potesse verificare la questione* — I would be grateful if you could look into the matter. For a firmer demand keep it impersonal and passive: *chiedo pertanto che venga emesso un rimborso completo* — I therefore request that a full refund be issued. Note *pertanto* (therefore) doing the formal work that *quindi* does in speech.

sections.heading: Structure and closing
sections.text: Build four short paragraphs: premise (who you are, what you bought), problem (what went wrong, in the passive), request (what you expect, by when), and close. Link them with *in merito a*, *di conseguenza*, *pertanto*, *in attesa di un Suo riscontro*. Sign off with *Cordiali saluti* for standard formality or *Distinti saluti* for the most formal register, followed by your full name.

body.scenario: You are the invited expert on a cultural radio programme discussing whether artificial intelligence will help or harm creative work. The presenter asks open, abstract questions and expects developed answers, not soundbites. Lay out a balanced position, cite an example, acknowledge the strongest counter-argument, and close with a forward-looking point when asked 'e nei prossimi dieci anni?'.
body.persona: A thoughtful radio presenter from Florence who asks probing follow-ups like 'in che senso?' and 'può fare un esempio concreto?' and gives you room to develop ideas
body.goal: Discuss an abstract topic fluently for several turns, structuring your reasoning with connectors and using the congiuntivo to frame opinions (*è probabile che… ritengo che…*)

questions.prompt: Complete: Pensavo che Marco ___ già partito.
questions.explanation: A past main verb (pensavo) requires the trapassato congiuntivo for an earlier action: che fosse partito. 'Sia partito' would need a present-tense trigger like 'penso'.

questions.prompt: Which is a correct third-type (irreale) hypothetical?
options: Se avessi avuto tempo, sarei venuto.
questions.explanation: The third type joins the trapassato congiuntivo (avessi avuto) with the condizionale passato (sarei venuto) to describe an unreal past. Option 2 is a second-type (present possibility).

questions.prompt: Complete: Accetto l'incarico, ___ i tempi siano realistici.
questions.explanation: 'A patto che' (provided that) introduces a condition and triggers the congiuntivo (siano). The other three state causes and take the indicative.

questions.prompt: In a formal email, 'eventualmente possiamo spostare la scadenza' means…
options: we will eventually move the deadline
we can possibly move the deadline, if need be
we have already moved the deadline
questions.explanation: 'Eventualmente' is a false friend: it means 'if need be / possibly', not 'eventually'. For 'eventually' use 'alla fine' or 'prima o poi'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: I dati sono stati pubblicati ieri.
questions.explanation: 'Sono stati pubblicati' (essere + past participle) is the passive; the subject 'i dati' receives the action. Italian can also form the passive with 'venire': 'i dati vengono pubblicati'.

questions.prompt: Complete: ___ fosse stanco, ha finito il progetto in tempo.
questions.explanation: 'Benché' (although) is a concessive conjunction that always takes the congiuntivo (fosse). The others are causal and take the indicative.
